{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZSG48A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC5SFI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 11, "title": "Implement BG1 direct color in Modes 3, 4 and 7", "body": "## Problem

Setting CGWSEL ($2130) bit 0 currently has no effect. Both planar 8-bpp BG1 rendering and Mode 7 always resolve nonzero pixel values through CGRAM, so programs requesting direct color display palette-dependent colors instead.

At baseline `7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd`:

- [`Ppu::bg_pixel`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L314) extracts the tilemap palette bits but discards them for 8-bpp pixels before calling `palette`.
- [`Ppu::mode7`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L366) also calls `palette` unconditionally for nonzero pixels.
- Existing [color-math regressions](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L700) exercise subscreen and fixed-color behavior, but do not exercise direct color. README explicitly lists direct color as unsupported.

This is a bounded missing input stage for the existing composition pipeline. The required 8-bpp pixel decoders already exist; implementing direct color does not require a new raster scheduler.

## Expected outcome

Implement direct color for BG1 in Modes 3 and 4, and Mode 7 with EXTBG disabled, within the existing scanline renderer.

Hardware semantics follow the [Fullsnes specification](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), specifically CGWSEL ($2130), BGMODE ($2105), and Direct Color Mode. This specification is already referenced in the repository's [hardware documentation provenance](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md#L273).

- CGWSEL bit 0 selects direct color for eligible BG1 pixels. Clearing it restores ordinary CGRAM lookup. Other CGWSEL bits retain their existing functions.
- For Modes 3/4, let the decoded pixel be `p = BBGGGRRR` and the tilemap palette field be `t = bgr` (tilemap bits 12–10). Construct five-bit components as:
  - `R5 = ((p & 7) << 2) | ((t & 1) << 1)` → `RRRr0`.
  - `G5 = (((p >> 3) & 7) << 2) | (((t >> 1) & 1) << 1)` → `GGGg0`.
  - `B5 = (((p >> 6) & 3) << 3) | (((t >> 2) & 1) << 2)` → `BBb00`.
  - The resulting BGR555 word is `R5 | (G5 << 5) | (B5 << 10)`.
- Mode 7 has no tilemap palette field; use `t = 0` for BG1 direct color.
- Raw pixel value zero remains transparent, including when a nonzero tilemap palette field would otherwise contribute color bits.
- Eligible nonzero direct-color pixels bypass CGRAM but retain their layer, priority, opacity and color-math eligibility. They participate in main/subscreen selection, windows, color math and brightness through the existing pipeline.
- BG2, objects and the backdrop continue using their existing color sources. CGRAM access/readback behavior is unchanged.

Scope is color selection and its integration. Non-goals are EXTBG implementation, Mode 7 transform corrections, offset-per-tile addressing, hires/interlace/overscan, pixel-fetch timing, mid-scanline register effects, or a general rewrite of color math.

## Context and reproduction

Create a Mode 3 BG1 tile whose sampled 8-bpp value is `0x01`, with tilemap palette field zero, full brightness, BG1 enabled on the main screen, and color math disabled. Set CGRAM entry 1 to blue (`0x7c00`).

With CGWSEL bit 0 clear, the pixel should be blue. With that bit set, it should instead use BGR555 `0x0004` (five-bit red level 4). Currently it remains blue. Changing the tilemap palette field to 1 should produce `0x0006` in direct-color mode; currently it still uses CGRAM.

Repeat through the Mode 4 path and a simple identity-transform Mode 7 scene. In Mode 7, pixel `0xff` should produce direct-color word `0x639c`; in Modes 3/4 with palette field 7, it should produce `0x73de`. These values precede brightness and framebuffer conversion.

Repository inspection found no direct-color tests. The supplied context lists no open Issues or recent improvements duplicating this behavior. External specification pages were not fetched during this repository-only evaluation, and no runtime validation is claimed here.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the specified BG1 color selection in both planar and Mode 7 rendering paths, preserving transparency before color conversion. Keep the implementation focused on the existing PPU architecture.
- [ ] Add original numerical tests covering all 256 pixel values and all eight Modes 3/4 palette fields. Derive expectations independently from the documented bit layout; do not call the implementation helper to calculate expected values. Test transparency separately from numerical conversion. Include fixed vectors for individual pixel/palette channel bits and the maximum values above.
- [ ] Add actual rendering regressions for Modes 3, 4 and 7. Cover direct-color enable/disable, independent contributions of all three tilemap palette bits, CGRAM mutation affecting palette mode but not eligible direct-color pixels, and raw-zero transparency with every palette field. Mode 7 tests must exercise its own rendering path with the palette contribution fixed to zero.
- [ ] Add integration cases for a direct-color pixel on the main screen and as a subscreen color-math operand, plus representative fixed-color math, window masking and reduced brightness. Assert independently calculated pixel values. Verify that enabling direct color does not change Mode 3/4 BG2, objects, backdrop colors, or paletted BG modes.
- [ ] Add an original, source-built guest test that programs the relevant registers and video memory through CPU execution in `Machine`, rather than only modifying PPU arrays. A small ROM generated from original Rust test source is sufficient and must run under `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Exercise each selected mode, use explicit frame/instruction bounds, and assert numeric framebuffer results. Document original code/data authorship and MIT provenance; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware. The new tests must demonstrate the baseline defect.
- [ ] Preserve existing diagnostic, color-math, tile-addressing, CPU/SPC, DMA/HDMA, audio and game regressions. Do not weaken hashes, durations or assertions to accommodate the change.
- [ ] Run the existing [README validation gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7b265281def439c97a18b006ad12e313198c1bcd/README.md#validate) before merge, including the following commands with the documented toolchain and browser prerequisites:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
cd web
npx playwright install chromium
npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

The browser gate includes the mandatory source-built Castle and Memory checks, their existing replay/progression assertions, and the diagnostic. Use only the pinned, licensed source-built hardware fixtures and cleared game builds described by repository provenance.

- [ ] Update README's direct-color support statement and report commands, results, fixture provenance/hashes, and any failures or skipped checks accurately. Passing this bounded coverage does not establish full PPU accuracy or commercial compatibility.

`ppu-color` remains partial after this Issue: comprehensive window-logic combinations, clipping/prevention interactions, subtraction/saturation, halving and brightness coverage still need work. Mode 7 EXTBG and transform edge behavior remain separate gaps. All other supplied inventory categories retain their existing scope and evidence; this Issue makes no completion claim for them.

## Optional validation

Additional original direct-color scenes combining tile flips, scrolling, mosaic and priority overlap. These do not replace the mandatory numerical and guest-execution tests.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
